status: Closed — branch-commit queue stale self-heal and durable audit verified 2026-09-05
area: Branch commit queue stale self-heal cross-actor boundary
finding: validate-branch-commit-queue asserted the source contract 'record.actorId !== input.actorId' and reported 'branch queue stale self-heal must not clean cross-actor locks'. Adjudication shows the guard was removed deliberately, not lost: commit 6301d93860bfa424d22a6be49af9fd36f7b188cc, 'fix(git): recover dead branch commit queues' (2026-07-29, codex-git-series-captain), removed both the cross-actor guard and the headMoved requirement in the same change. Keeping either meant an orphan lock left by a crashed peer could deadlock the queue permanently: reclamation required HEAD to have moved, but nothing could move HEAD while the lock was held. That is the same deadlock shape as an orphaned .git/index.lock.
expectedBehavior: Reclaiming a dead owner's lock is the purpose of self-heal, so the bound cannot be the owner's identity. The replacement bound is provable owner death (isBranchCommitQueueOwnerAlive over the recorded ownerPid, with only false or unknown treated as reclaimable), plus a staleness threshold, plus a durable audit record naming the reclaiming actor. The validator anchor was updated to assert exactly that bound. The protection was replaced, not weakened, and the anchor now describes the contract the code actually holds.
evidenceOrRepro: git show 6301d9386 -- packages/cli/src/commands/git-governance/implementation/branch-commit-window.ts shows both conditions removed together. After re-anchoring on the current bound, node --strip-types scripts/validate-branch-commit-queue.ts --mode validate reports ok, with the busy and race retry codes, the queue evidence schema id, the lock ownerPid record, the ATM_BRANCH_COMMIT_QUEUE_STALE_SELF_HEALED audit reason and branch-commit-queue-stale-cleanup.jsonl all still required. Two unrelated anchor defects in the same validator, a frozen file list and a formatter-dependent quote style, were repaired under ATM-GOV-0354.
followUp: None for the guard itself. The remaining risk is that the durable audit is the only record of a cross-actor reclamation, so any future change that drops branch-commit-queue-stale-cleanup.jsonl or the reclaiming actorId from that record removes the last trace of who reclaimed whose lock; both are now anchored in the validator to prevent that.
